title: ruled
intention: Akien's RULED marker fires the ruling door in the same act he types it — /RULED <id> is the marker's front door, so a confirmation can never again sit in conversation waiting for CC to notice it.
why: n=2 measured 2026-08-15: both confirmations of the authority ruling reached the door only because CC noticed 'so /ruled ...' in conversation and hand-ran bin/cmd/ruling confirm — the marker enforced by CC's attention, which is policy doing physics' job (Law 4). Akien, verbatim: 'and we should add a /RULED since i seem to keep using it :)'. The declined alternative is already measured at the ruling machine's edge (b): lexical marker detection fires on 28.5% of 855 real prompts; an explicit skill invocation has a zero false-fire rate by construction.
traces_to: Law 4 (the marker reaches the door because he typed it, not because CC was paying attention), Law 6 (confirmation stays his: the recorded verbatim is what he typed — the boundary the ruling machine's edge (f) settled, untouched)

falsifier.proves_green: skill-class invariants: proved (proofs beside the skill a hollow build could not pass — id resolution, refuse-by-listing, evidence-recorded-verbatim, the no-packet loud refusal — run bare and under the tester) + feeds back to origin on failure. Extra gate of the class: the cairnmap derivation gate — ships only when the help renders it from its charter AND node_classes/skill.json's roster carries it (in scope of this build).
falsifier.proves_red: /RULED <id> leaves the packet confirmed with his invocation recorded verbatim as the evidence, verify green+ruled, in one turn with no hand-run confirm; bare /RULED lists the open unmarked packets; /RULED <nothing-matches> refuses loudly naming the store searched. Wrong-intent tell: if his markers keep landing as bare prose CC must notice, the front door is not where he reaches.
falsifier.horizon: One thin skill over cairn/machines/ruling/'s existing confirm and verify verbs — no new intake, no new store, no new confirmation authority. Bounded OUT and left where it is filed: nothing yet makes a ruling packet EXIST when he rules in conversation (the machine's edge (b)); /RULED confirms what exists and says so loudly when nothing does.

how: Build /ruled skill: Akien types 'cairn ruled <id>' and it fires the ruling door in the same act. The skill reads the ruling, opens the packet, and fires.
